My Monday summary email shows up on Tuesday morning, every week. I'm in Sydney.
Colleagues in London get theirs on Monday as expected. Our account settings
have the right time zone for each of us.

Investigation could not locate the relevant scheduler/job source in the repository (searches for related terms returned no matches, and the expected file paths do not exist in this checkout), so no specific file can be pinpointed. The report itself describes a timezone-handling bug: users in timezones behind UTC (e.g., Sydney) receive their Monday summary a day late compared to users in timezones closer to UTC (e.g., London), despite correct per-account timezone settings. This points to the weekly summary scheduling logic not correctly converting/localizing the send time per user's timezone.

label: question
file: none

Investigation could not locate any scheduler or job source related to weekly summary emails in this repository: all searches for relevant terms returned no matches, and the two candidate file paths checked (src/scheduler/sendWeeklySummary.js, src/jobs/weeklySummary.js) do not exist in this checkout. Since the rules require every non-question label to name a file that an earlier step actually showed, and no such file was found, this cannot be filed as a bug against a specific source.

The report describes a plausible timezone-handling issue: a user in Sydney (behind UTC) receives their Monday summary a day late compared to a user in London (closer to UTC), despite correct per-account timezone settings. This is worth tracking, but confirming it requires locating the actual scheduling/send-time logic, which was not found here. Recommend follow-up to identify the correct module (possibly under a different name or in another repository/service) before re-triaging as a bug.
